core.title: Plan trains as production orchestration, not test infrastructure
core.given: A train is involved in any planner artifact (plan, wagon, WMBT, acceptance or doc)
core.when: the planner specifies, references or describes that train
core.then: Treat the train as production orchestration, not test infrastructure: located in the stack's production train directory and executed by the stack's production executor of a train.
prefer: Name the stack's production executor of a train as the executor.
Reference the stack's train implementation-patterns documentation as the place where train implementation patterns are described.
avoid: Planning trains as test infrastructure (fixtures, harnesses, test-only helpers) or placing them under test directories.
Stating an executor or location for trains other than the stack's production executor in the production train directory.
core.why: Trains are production orchestration executed by the stack's production executor in the production train directory; classifying them as test infrastructure misstates what they are and where they live.
evidence: Planner artifacts involving a train treat it as production code in the production train directory, executed by the production executor of a train.
No planner artifact describes a train as test infrastructure or locates it under a test path.
verification: Resolve the expected train location, executor and patterns document from the profile (production train directory, train-executor construct, conventions tree); the check must not hard-code them.

Activation requires train-specific context (a train term, the executor's name, or a train artifact/location); generic orchestration terms or plan-path signals alone are supporting signals only and never activate the rule on their own.
The planning-phase fact scopes the audience (planner authoring artifacts) only; it is not a narrowing condition on the obligation.
Whether an artifact frames or places a train as test infrastructure rather than production code requires judgement; it is not decided from paths alone.
Term aliases that bind the executor's name to 'the production executor of a train' are realization data; the check compares against the profile's train-executor construct, not a hard-coded name.

values: file under the production train directory
train framed or placed as test infrastructure

fires: Any planner artifact (plan, wagon, WMBT, acceptance, doc) that involves a train, whether or not it explicitly discusses placement or executor.
A plan proposes putting train orchestration under a test directory or describes it as test fixtures/harness.
Docs for a train name an executor or location other than the stack's production executor in the production train directory.
doesNotFire: Planner artifacts with no train involved, even if they use generic words like 'orchestration' or live under a plan path.
Acceptance tests that exercise a train are themselves test code; the rule still applies to how the train they exercise is classified.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where production trains live; instantiates the core's 'production train directory' in then, avoid[1], why, evidence[0], fires[2] and the location half of activation.
The stack's construct (name and module) of the production executor of a train; instantiates the core's 'production executor of a train' and joins the activation trigger terms under that name.
Name pattern that identifies a train definition artifact; the concrete train-artifact activation signal.
Where the stack's convention documents live; where train implementation patterns are documented, referenced by prefer[1].

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's concrete construct (name and module) of the production executor of a train.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: idiom has route/auth/error/validation/import/nesting and markup constructs only; tooling.test_runner names the test runner, not the production executor of a train.

proposedKeys.meaning: Suffix or name pattern of a train definition artifact.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: suffix.<file_kind> params (source, unit_test, acceptance_test, e2e_test, markup, plan_artifact, config) include no train kind; a train definition is production orchestration, not a plan artifact.

proposedKeys.meaning: Tree or file where the stack's convention documents live; where train implementation patterns are documented.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roots names only config, source, test, e2e, plan and scan trees, and no other group says where the stack's convention documents live.

neutralityNotes: Train, wagon and WMBT are ATDD methodology vocabulary (train/wagon/wmbt are urn artifact params in the closed vocabulary) and are kept in the core; they are not stack specifics. Everything concrete is carried by four proposed profile keys: the train directory (python/trains/), the executor construct (TrainRunner, python/trains/runner.py), the train-artifact naming (**/*.train.yaml) and the train-patterns document (atdd/coder/conventions/train.convention.yaml); the closed vocabulary had no fitting key for any of them. activation.facts[1] is a path_glob in bun.json, but the neutral fact vocabulary has no path_glob, so it is expressed as a file_kind fact whose concrete patterns come from the profile. The term id train_runner and the SESSION-12 lineage marker are realization details and remain Bun-only. 'unless' is empty in bun.json and stays empty; no exception was dropped or added.
